content.text: [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/selling-ebooks-without-paypal-which-architecture-actually-works-2|Selling Ebooks]] a digital product should be a simple transaction. You build something valuable — an ebook, a course, a Notion template, a font family, a preset pack, a beat — and someone pays you for access to it. The file transfers. The transaction completes. But for millions of creators, the [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/usdt-payment-gateways-digital-products-what-actually-how-3|COREMERCH guide to payment]] layer is where [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/everything-you-need-know-about-cloudflare-workers-crypto-5|everything]] breaks down. Stripe is unavailable. PayPal flags the account. Gumroad holds the payout. The workarounds stop working. What actually works is a sovereign commerce stack: a static storefront on GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages, automatic payment verification through NOWPayments, and delivery triggered by a webhook the moment the transaction confirms on-chain. No platform intermediary. No payout schedule. No geography filter. The customer owns the storefront code, the order history, the customer list, and the product files. COREMERCH has no access after deployment.

This post is part of the COREMERCH infrastructure series. For the complete foundation — every component, every configuration step, and the full deployment sequence — read the pillar guide: How to Start Selling Digital Products with Crypto Payments at https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/automated-digital-product-delivery-crypto-explained-digital-creators-2. That guide covers the complete architecture that this post builds on.
content.title: How to Start Selling Digital Products with Crypto Payments

content.text: What This Actually Is and Why It Matters: Crypto payment

The automated delivery pipeline for digital products follows a specific sequence that eliminates every manual step. A buyer visits the storefront, selects a product, and initiates payment. The checkout displays a QR code with the exact wallet address and payment amount in their chosen cryptocurrency, converted from USD at the current exchange rate via live price feeds. The buyer sends the payment from their wallet. NOWPayments monitors the blockchain and detects the incoming transaction within seconds of broadcast. When the transaction receives sufficient confirmations on-chain, NOWPayments fires a webhook to your Cloudflare Worker or Google Apps Script endpoint. The backend verifies the payment amount, confirms the transaction hash on the blockchain directly, logs the order, generates a receipt, and sends the download link to the buyer's email address.
How the Architecture Works Under the Hood

The architecture of crypto payment gateways involves the integration of various components, including a frontend for user interaction, a backend for logic and data storage, and a cryptocurrency payment processor. For instance, COREMERCH utilizes GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for backend logic, and NOWPayments for automatic on-chain crypto payment verification. This setup enables automatic product delivery and ensures that creators have full ownership of their data and commerce infrastructure.
Who This Is Built For and Why

This infrastructure is specifically designed for digital creators in regions where access to traditional payment gateways is limited or restricted, such as Kenya, Ghana, and Zimbabwe. These creators can sell ebooks, courses, templates, fonts, presets, beats, plugins, and software but face challenges in collecting payments. The sovereign commerce infrastructure provided by COREMERCH is built to address these challenges, offering a reliable and efficient solution for digital transactions.
Empower your digital sales with sovereign commerce infrastructure.
The Components That Make It Work Together

Key components include hosting services like GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages, backend logic tools such as Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script, and cryptocurrency payment processors like NOWPayments. Additionally, services like Supabase or Google Sheets are used for order storage, and Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 for file delivery. These components work together seamlessly to provide a comprehensive commerce solution that is both secure and efficient.
How to Use This Knowledge to Deploy Today

To deploy a crypto payment gateway for digital products, creators can start by selecting the appropriate components based on their specific needs. COREMERCH offers pre-configured stacks like the Sovereign Starter Stack and the Edge Commerce Stack, which can be deployed within 48 hours. Alternatively, creators can opt for the Complete Builder Kit, which provides all the necessary documentation and templates to set up a custom solution. By following a step-by-step approach and leveraging the right tools and resources, creators can quickly establish a functional and sovereign commerce infrastructure.
How do I sell an ebook online without PayPal or Stripe?

The fastest path to your first sovereign digital product sale is a three-step process. First, create a NOWPayments account — configure your wallet addresses for USDT on Tron and Bitcoin as starting points, generate your API key, and set the webhook endpoint URL. Second, choose your stack: Stack 01 uses GitHub Pages plus Google Apps Script and takes most creators four to six hours following the Sovereign Blueprint at $47; Stack 02 uses Cloudflare Pages plus Workers plus Supabase and is deployed by COREMERCH in 48 hours with the Edge Commerce Stack at $197. Third, upload your product files, set your prices in USD, and run a complete mainnet test transaction before promoting.
Bypass traditional payment restrictions with crypto gateways.

Your Deployment Checklist

To deploy a crypto payment gateway, follow these steps: select a hosting service, choose a backend logic tool, set up a cryptocurrency payment processor, configure order storage and file delivery services, and test the entire setup to ensure seamless functionality. Additionally, consider opting for a pre-configured stack or the Complete Builder Kit to streamline the process. Ensure all components are properly integrated and that you have a clear understanding of how each part works together to provide a comprehensive commerce solution.
